summary:
RESEARCH ONLY, 2026-10-17. Nothing was downloaded, bought, signed up for, installed or edited. Sources are vendor pricing and terms pages, GitHub and Hugging Face model cards, and papers. tripo3d.ai and openai.com returned HTTP 403, so their figures come from mirrors and aggregators and are marked as such. csm.ai did not resolve in DNS.

QUOTING NOTE: My operating rules allow one short verbatim quote per answer. Every other licence term below is a close paraphrase with its section number and URL. Copy the verbatim text from those URLs into PLAN.md before relying on it. The one quote is from the Google Terms of Service (effective 30 Jul 2026, https://policies.google.com/terms): "Google won't claim ownership over that content."

VERDICT: No AI route beats real photographs for a landscaping business. The best result for the PHOTOREAL bar is the existing species-geometry plan, textured from the owner's own photos of the cultivars he actually installs. AI should process those photos and fill short-term gaps. It should not be the source of the plants.

Why:
1) Botanical fidelity is the weak point, and it is what this business sells. The only expert study found is Theidel, JoDLA 11-2026, doi:10.14627/537770002 (https://gispoint.de/fileadmin/user_upload/paper_gis_open/DLA_2026/537770002.pdf). Seven landscape experts rated a ChatGPT-4o planting image:
- Overall: 2.34/5.
- Botany and geometry: 2.21/5.
- Professional trustworthiness: 1.57/5, with 5 of 7 experts giving the lowest score.
- All 7 preferred a conventional visualisation.
- The failures were species identity, morphology, phenology and scale, not editing artefacts.
2) Image-to-3D services fuse thin leaves, needles and blades into lumpy shells. No vendor publishes foliage results.
3) Consumer image apps give no seed. Batches are not reproducible, and multi-view sets are not 3D-consistent.
4) Gemini and ChatGPT outputs are licence-safe for a public repo and runtime use, because the user owns them per the vendor terms. They are probably not copyrightable, though: the US Copyright Office says prompts alone do not create authorship, and Canada is unsettled. Competitors could lift them freely. The owner's own photos are protected.
5) The owner's real advantage is access to nurseries and job sites. Photos of the exact cultivars he installs are both more accurate and honest marketing ("what you see is what we plant").

HOW AI COMPLEMENTS THE OWNER'S PHOTOS:
(a) Build-time processing with licence-clean open tools:
- BiRefNet matting (MIT).
- Marigold intrinsic decomposition for albedo and roughness (Apache-2.0 code, RAIL++-M weights).
- Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0; the larger sizes are non-commercial).
- Materialize and DeepBump for normal and height maps (GPL-3 tools; the GPL does not bind the output images).
- Real-ESRGAN (BSD-3), for bark and mulch tiles only.
(b) A seasonal bridge. It is mid-October in Ontario. Evergreens, bark and grasses in autumn state can be photographed now. Summer foliage and bloom for deciduous trees, shrubs and perennials can only be captured from about mid-May to September 2027. Until then, approved browser-generated sheets (route R1) or CC0 iNaturalist photos can fill atlas cells. Mark them in the manifest and replace them later.
(c) Low-risk non-botanical fill: mulch, leaf-litter and bark tiles.
(d) Optionally, octahedral impostors baked from our own models for phone LOD2 (R14).

ROUTES TO REJECT:
- AI whole-plant billboards (R2) and AI orbit-video splats (R16).
- Buying an image-to-3D subscription (R3–R9). At most it gives clipped-evergreen hulls, which the procedural plan already builds in about 300 triangles.
- Gaussian splats (R15) are the most photographic way to capture real foliage, but they bake in lighting, do not take part in sun shadows, are not rendered by three-gpu-pathtracer Photo mode, and cost MBs per plant. The 273-plant showcase cannot use them. At most they suit one or two hero specimens, and only after an owner decision.

CHEAP TEST BEFORE ANY SPEND (needs owner approval at each step):
1. Pick 3 species: 'Annabelle', 'Smaragd' and 'Karl Foerster'.
2. Build each species' atlas cells three ways:
   - the owner's phone photos (evergreen and grass now);
   - one approved Gemini or ChatGPT batch;
   - CC0 iNaturalist photos.
3. Render each at the Bed close-up, Corner and Front cameras. Ask 3–5 homeowners to pick "photo vs render" blind.
4. Optionally upload one owner photo to a free image-to-3D tier. Free tiers make outputs public under CC BY or vendor-owned, so the photo should be one the owner is happy to publish.

PRICE SHEET (all purchases need owner approval):
- Image apps:
  - Google AI Pro: about US$19.99 or CA$26.99 per month. AI Ultra: US$249.99 per month.
  - ChatGPT Go: about US$8. Plus: US$20. Pro: US$100–200 per month.
  - Gemini's visible watermark can be switched off in settings since 14 Aug 2026. SynthID stays.
- Image-to-3D:
  - Meshy: Pro US$20/mo (1,000 credits; about 20–25 credits per image-to-3D), Premium US$40, Ultra US$100, Studio US$70.
  - Tripo: Pro US$19.90/mo, or US$13.93/mo billed annually (3,000 credits, about 120 models). Max US$89.90. Team US$329.70.
  - Hyper3D Rodin: Creator US$30/mo or US$24/mo yearly. Business US$120/mo or US$96/mo yearly.
- Other tools:
  - Adobe Substance 3D Texturing plan (includes Sampler's Image to Material): US$24.99/mo, or US$17.49/mo on an annual plan.
  - Imposter Cards Blender add-on: US$25 standard, US$50 Advanced.
  - Calibrite ColorChecker list prices: Classic Mini about US$74, Passport Photo 2 about US$119.
- Cloud GPU for TRELLIS.2, which needs a 24 GB+ GPU (the owner's RTX 5070 has 12 GB): RunPod A100 80GB about US$1.19–1.89 per hour, RTX 4090 about US$0.34–0.74 per hour.
- Metered Higgsfield gpt_image_2 is the agent-wide default elsewhere. It is excluded here unless the owner approves.

LICENCE FLAGS THE PLANNER MUST CARRY:
- Hunyuan3D 2.1 Community License, Exhibit A item 12: machine-generated content placed in public must be conspicuously labelled as machine-generated. This conflicts with an unlabelled photoreal site.
- nvdiffrast (inside TRELLIS.2's pipeline) is licensed for non-commercial use only (§3.3). TRELLIS v1's diffoctreerast derives from Inria code, and the Inria Gaussian Splatting licence is non-commercial.
- Meshy ToS §2.4 forbids removing AI-generation identifiers from outputs. Our build strips metadata, so that would breach it.
- Meshy and Tripo free tiers: the vendor owns the outputs or keeps rights to them, and outputs are public or CC BY.
- Excluded on licence grounds: BRIA RMBG-2.0 (CC BY-NC), Ubisoft CHORD (research-only), Postshot Free (non-commercial).
- The repo checkout has no LICENSE file, so committed owner assets default to all rights reserved. GitHub's terms let others view and fork public repos, and §D.4 lets GitHub use content to train its AI features. That is a minor point against Hunyuan §5(b) and the Google terms clause on using outputs to develop models.

COMPATIBILITY: Every route keys assets by species id at render time, so saved designs need no migration. The phone tiers (balanced at most LOD1, constrained LOD2) and showcase forced LOD0 work with R1, R10–R14. R2, R13 and R15 cannot serve as LOD0 for stills.

OPEN OR UNVERIFIED:
- Tripo's and Rodin's ToS wording on output ownership.
- The Postshot Indie price.
- Luma Genie's status: its page no longer describes 3D generation.
- CSM Cube's status: Google's acquisition of CSM closed 24 Jan 2026, and csm.ai did not resolve.
- Cultivar accuracy of Gemini and ChatGPT for these specific cultivars. Untested; the cheap test above covers it.
- ChatGPT app transparency: it does not reliably output real alpha. Use a white/black difference matte or a green key.
- Gemini's interactive 3D feature renders code-built WebGL scenes with no GLB export. It is useless for assets.

routes.name: R1. Species detail images generated in the browser (Gemini or ChatGPT) as atlas sources
routes.species_coverage:
All 26 species can be prompted at species level. Expected reliability (inferred, not tested):
- Good: sugar and red maple leaf, redbud heart leaf, hosta leaf, coneflower and black-eyed Susan heads, bark tiles.
- Medium: serviceberry, dogwood, lilac, ninebark and hydrangea leaves; Annabelle floret; panicle hydrangea panicle; bergamot whorl; daylily strap leaf; ostrich fern pinnae.
- Weak (cultivar or species traits AI tends to blur):
  - Smaragd's flat vertical scale sprays come out as generic arborvitae.
  - Karl Foerster's narrow upright plume comes out as a generic feather grass.
  - Picea pungens' glaucous cast.
  - Pinus strobus' 5-needle fascicles.
  - Taxus x media's flat needles.
  - Boxwood's tiny leaves.
  - The small flower spikes of catmint and salvia.
  - Switchgrass and little bluestem panicles.
Foliage and flower colour depends on the cultivar for ninebark, spirea, salvia and daylily, so the owner must name the cultivars he sells.
routes.realism:
A single leaf or flower can look photographic at 1–2K. No published test of single-organ botanical accuracy exists.
The only expert evaluation found (Theidel, JoDLA 11-2026, https://gispoint.de/fileadmin/user_upload/paper_gis_open/DLA_2026/537770002.pdf) rated a ChatGPT-4o planting visualisation:
- Botany and geometry: 2.21/5.
- Trustworthiness: 1.57/5.
- Failures came from species identity, morphology, phenology and scale.
AI 'impossible flora' such as ten-foot hostas is documented at https://cswr.hds.harvard.edu/news/2025/02/fighting-new-invasive-species-ais-impossible-flora.
Practical defects:
- Lighting is baked in: highlights, cast shadows and boosted saturation must be removed before the image can serve as albedo.
- There is no seed, so sheets for one species drift in hue and leaf shape between runs.
- Neither app guarantees tileable edges, so bark and mulch tiles need offset-and-repair, for example with Materialize or Sampler.
- ChatGPT does not reliably give a real alpha channel (https://community.openai.com/t/having-trouble-getting-transparent-backgrounds-in-chatgpt-images/1380143). Gemini shows a fake checkerboard (https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/how-can-i-make-the-background-transparent/111698).
routes.licence:
Google Terms of Service, effective 30 Jul 2026 (https://policies.google.com/terms):
- Verbatim: "Google won't claim ownership over that content."
- The same terms forbid misleading others into thinking generative-AI content was made by a human, and using output from Google's AI services to develop ML models (paraphrase).
Google Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy, last modified 17 Dec 2024 (https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy):
- §4.5 bars misrepresenting the provenance of generated content as solely human-made in order to deceive.
- No clause on watermark removal.
Visible Gemini watermark:
- Since 14 Aug 2026, the 'Media watermark' setting can turn it off. It is on by default and hidden where law mandates labels. SynthID stays (https://pcworld.com/article/3213409/google-now-lets-you-nix-visible-gemini-image-watermarks.html).
OpenAI Terms of Use, effective 1 Jan 2026 (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use; mirror https://conductatlas.com/platform/openai/terms-of-use-row/openai-assigns-output-ownership-to-user/), paraphrased:
- As between the user and OpenAI, and as far as the law allows, the user owns Output, and OpenAI assigns its rights in Output 'if any'.
- Output may not be unique.
- The assignment excludes other users' output and Third Party Output.
- ChatGPT images carry C2PA metadata, which re-encoding strips. No OpenAI rule against stripping it was found.
Copyrightability:
- US Copyright Office Part 2 (29 Jan 2025): prompts alone are not enough for authorship (https://ipwatchdog.com/2025/01/29/part-two-copyright-office-ai-report-says-creative-prompting-doesnt-constitute-authorship/).
- Canada is unsettled: the SURYAST challenge is pending at the Federal Court (https://www.musicpublishing.ca/news/2026-7-22-music-publishers-canada-intervenes-in-landmark-federal-court-case-on-ai-and-copyright).
Result: the owner may commit these images to the public repo and serve them, but probably cannot stop others reusing them.
routes.cost:
Gemini:
- Free tier: limited Pro uses, about 1K output by default.
- Google AI Pro: about US$19.99 or CA$26.99 per month (2K output; third-party sources say about 100 Pro images a day).
- AI Ultra: US$249.99 per month (4K).
ChatGPT (unofficial limits):
- Free: about 2–3 images a day.
- Go: about US$8. Plus: US$20. Pro: US$100–200.
A 26-species run of about 150–250 images including retries fits in one month of Gemini AI Pro or ChatGPT Plus.
Metered Higgsfield gpt_image_2 is excluded unless the owner approves it.
Labour: about 1–2 hours per species to cut out, de-light, calibrate and review.
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve each generation batch, per the browser-flow rule.
- Choose the provider and plan.
- Decide on the Gemini watermark setting.
- Name the exact cultivar installed for each species.
- Give botanical sign-off on every sheet.
- Approve provenance labels in the manifest (for example 'AI-generated, Gemini, 2026-10-xx') and a rule to replace them with his own photos in 2027.
routes.web_fit:
Identical to PLAN.md:
- Shared WebP or KTX2 atlases of 1024²–2048² with 12–16 cells.
- A leaf-cluster cell needs about 128–256 px, so Gemini's 1K output is enough. Use 2K for bark.
- About 5.3 MiB of GPU memory per 1024² RGBA8 atlas with mips, or roughly a quarter of that with KTX2.
- No runtime code change. The build step adds cutout, colour dilation and calibration, which are already planned.
- No effect on the phone tiers.
routes.risks:
- Wrong cultivar or organ detail rendered photoreal sets false homeowner expectations. Possible consumer-protection exposure; not researched in depth.
- Batches cannot be reproduced.
- Colour drifts between sheets.
- Baked lighting.
- The images are probably not copyrightable.
- Free quotas change often.
- The over-smooth, too-symmetric 'AI look' is the tell homeowners notice.

routes.name: R2. Browser-generated whole-plant cutouts as billboards or view-set sprites
routes.what:
Generate one isolated eye-level image per species, for example a 3 ft Annabelle hydrangea on white. Edit it into 3–7 rotated views, matte them, and render them as:
- camera-facing billboards;
- crossed cards; or
- view-indexed sprites, where the shader picks the nearest of N azimuth views.
The concept matches two industry precedents:
- ArchVision RPC, a set of photographed basis views (https://scholars.uky.edu/en/publications/automated-basis-view-and-match-point-selection-for-the-archvision/).
- PRO Landscape's 2D photo-imaging library of real plants (https://www.totallandscapecare.com/business/article/15041829/exploring-landscape-design-software-programs).
routes.species_coverage:
All 26 in principle.
- Least bad for compact, near-symmetric forms: boxwood, yew, Smaragd, both hydrangeas, hosta, grasses and perennials.
- Unacceptable for trees seen from the Above or Overview cameras.
routes.realism:
Seen from the single viewpoint it was made for, a good cutout is the most photographic option there is, which is why landscaping photo-imaging tools use cutouts. DeckCraft is an orbiting 3D viewer, though:
- The card visibly rotates with the camera.
- Top-down views collapse.
- Lighting is baked and disagrees with DeckCraft's sun and HDRI.
- There is no self-shadowing or parallax.
- AI-generated alternate views are not 3D-consistent, so they pop when the view switches.
Verdict: fails at the Bed close-up and the Corner orbit. Usable at best as far LOD2.
routes.licence: Same as R1: Google Terms of Service (https://policies.google.com/terms) and OpenAI Terms of Use (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use). The user owns outputs per vendor terms. They are probably not copyrightable.
routes.cost: As R1, plus about 8 views × 26 species, roughly 200–400 generations including retries.
routes.owner_actions: As R1, plus approve every view set and a per-species visual check.
routes.web_fit:
- 2 triangles per plant, but the texture memory is high: 8 views at 256×512 RGBA8 with mips is about 5.6 MiB per species, about 145 MiB for all 26.
- Usable only with KTX2, 4 views, and only the species present in a design.
- Alpha-tested overdraw is costly on tile-based phone GPUs.
- Conflicts with the plan's baked billboard-cloud LOD2, which is consistently lit from our own models.
- Cannot be LOD0, so it cannot serve showcase stills.
routes.risks:
- Obvious CG tell when orbiting.
- Lighting mismatch.
- Inconsistent views pop.
- Quota and approval load.
- Homeowner-expectation risk.
- New runtime shader code.

routes.name: R3. Meshy image-to-3D (Meshy 6/7, browser app)
routes.what: Upload an owner photo or an approved AI image and receive a textured PBR GLB. The built-in remesh tool sets the polygon target. Multi-image input is supported.
routes.realism:
Searches on 2026-10-17 found no vendor or third-party foliage tests.
- Meshy's own 3D-printing guide says sub-millimetre features such as hair strands come out as fragile geometry (https://www.meshy.ai/blog/best-ai-tools-for-3d-printing).
- Research says sub-voxel structures are smoothed out or merged in Hunyuan3D-class latents, with vine branches merging (SAM3D-Part, arXiv 2609.15639, per a search excerpt; the PDF was too large to fetch).
- A CSM reviewer says thin or complex geometry reconstructs poorly.
- Tripo's own blog suggests AI meshes for background plants and manual modelling for hero plants.
- A third-party listing claims a 'meshy-6 oak' with dense foliage clusters (https://www.summerengine.com/asset-store/realistic-mature-oak-tree-9fca7577). Unverified.
Expected result: leaves fused into a lumpy shell with the photo projected on it, shadows included. Reads as topiary at Corner distance; fails at the Bed close-up.
routes.licence:
Meshy Terms, last updated 19 Sep 2026 (https://www.meshy.ai/terms-of-use), paraphrased:
- §3.2 Free plan: Meshy owns all rights in Customer Output and makes it available under CC BY 4.0, with credit to Meshy.
- §3.2 Paid plan: the customer owns the output and may keep it private.
- §2.4: users must not remove, alter or tamper with AI-generation identifiers (watermarks or metadata).
- §2.6: no competing products, and outputs may not train competing AI models.
- §2.9: Meshy may train on non-Enterprise users' content.
- §3.3: Community posts are CC0.
Meshy's docs table (https://docs.meshy.ai/en/webapp/pricing) says Free-plan users own outputs. That contradicts the ToS, and the ToS controls.
routes.cost:
Plans (https://www.meshy.ai/pricing):
- Free: 100 credits/mo, up to 10 assets, CC BY.
- Pro: US$20/mo (US$10 first month), 1,000 credits.
- Premium: US$40, 3,000 credits.
- Ultra: US$100, 8,000 credits.
- Studio: US$70 (team).
- Enterprise: custom.
- The FAQ says annual billing is 20% off.
Credits per generation:
- Image to 3D: 20 credits on Meshy 6, 25 on Meshy 7 (webapp docs). The API docs list 30 with texture.
- AI texturing: 10 credits.
A 26-species run with 3 tries each is about 1,600–2,000 credits: Premium for one month (about US$40) or Pro for two months.
routes.owner_actions:
- Account sign-up.
- Approve the plan purchase.
- Approve each upload. Uploads may train Meshy's models unless on Enterprise.
- Accept that §2.4 constrains our pipeline's metadata stripping.
- Review outputs.
routes.web_fit:
- Outputs are GLB with PBR textures at 2K–4K (8K optional).
- Each asset ships its own texture set, so it must be re-baked into the shared atlases.
- Decimate with gltf-transform or meshoptimizer to the plan budgets: shrub 3.5k/1.2k/≤150 triangles, clipped evergreen 3k/900/≤120, tree 12k/3.5k/≤300.
- Opaque shells avoid alpha-test cost, which is good for phones.
- About 1–3 hours of Blender cleanup and rescaling per species. AI meshes are not to metric scale.
routes.risks:
- Fused foliage and baked shadows in the texture.
- §2.4 identifier rule against our metadata-stripping build.
- Training on uploads.
- Results vary between runs.
- Terms change frequently: the current ToS dates from 19 Sep 2026.

routes.name: R4. Tripo image-to-3D (Tripo 3.x, browser app)
routes.what: Image or multi-view to a textured GLB with 'smart low-poly' quad topology.
routes.species_coverage: Same as R3: shells for clipped or dense forms and hydrangea or coneflower heads. Not usable for trees, grasses, the fern or fine-textured shrubs and perennials at close range.
routes.realism:
A HackerNoon test by a Meshy-team author on 3 generators (https://hackernoon.com/how-i-stress-tested-3-ai-3d-generators-on-the-same-inputs-what-the-numbers-actually-show) found:
- Tripo had the best geometry and cleanest topology.
- Tripo v3.1 image-to-3D took about 99 s, at about US$0.18 per call.
No foliage tests were found. Tripo's own guidance says AI plant meshes suit background filler, and hero plants should be modelled by hand (blog excerpt via search; the page returned 403).
routes.licence:
The official pages returned 403, so these come from search excerpts and aggregators.
- Tripo pricing page: free-plan models are public under CC BY 4.0.
- Tripo help page, citing ToS §5.2.1: Tripo retains all rights in Free users' inputs and outputs.
- Paid users have full rights to use, modify, distribute and commercially exploit their models, and Tripo does not train on paid users' inputs and outputs. Help page: https://www.tripo3d.ai/help/privacy-policy/how-to-use-tripo-models-commercially.
- CostBench lists the free tier as non-commercial (https://costbench.com/software/ai-3d-generation/tripo-ai/).
Result: the free tier is unclear; paid is fine.
routes.cost:
- Pro: US$19.90/mo, or US$13.93/mo billed annually; 3,000 credits, up to about 120 models (official page per search excerpt).
- Free: 200–300 credits (sources disagree).
- Max: US$89.90/mo.
- Team: US$329.70/mo, raised from about US$110 on 24 Aug 2026 per CostBench.
One Pro month covers a 26-species test.
routes.owner_actions:
- Sign up.
- Approve the purchase.
- Approve uploads. Free-tier outputs are public, so no owner photos he wants to keep private.
- Review outputs.
routes.web_fit:
- Same as R3.
- Quad low-poly output eases decimation.
- Re-bake textures into shared atlases.
- 1–3 hours of cleanup per species.
routes.risks:
- Fused foliage.
- Free-tier rights conflict.
- Price volatility (200% top-tier rise in Aug 2026).
- Terms could not be read first-hand.

routes.name: R5. Hyper3D Rodin (Deemos), image-to-3D
routes.what: High-fidelity image-to-3D with PBR. According to a third-party source, credits are charged on download rather than on generation.
routes.species_coverage: Same as R3: shells for boxwood, yew and Smaragd hulls and flower heads only.
routes.realism: Third-party guides rank Rodin highest for geometry fidelity (https://www.seeles.ai/compare/rodin). No foliage evidence was found. The representation limits on thin structures (see R3) apply.
routes.licence:
Hyper3D Terms, undated 'current version' (https://hyper3d.ai/legal/terms), paraphrased:
- There is no express clause assigning Output ownership.
- §5: for Rodin, Deemos will not limit the user's use of Output, subject to its agreements, applicable law and third-party terms, and makes no representation that Output is copyrightable.
- Output can be set to private.
- §6.1 excludes Prompts and Output from Deemos's own IP.
- ChatAvatar free output is personal use only, which is not relevant here.
routes.cost:
Plans (https://hyper3d.ai/pricing):
- Free: direct credits at US$1.5 each.
- Creator: US$30/mo, or US$24/mo billed yearly (US$288); about 60 models.
- Business: US$120/mo, or US$96/mo billed yearly (US$1,152); about 416 models.
- Education: discounted.
- Enterprise: custom.
A third-party source says a Gen-2 download costs about 40 credits.
routes.owner_actions:
- Sign up.
- Approve the purchase.
- Mark outputs private.
- Ideally get written confirmation from Deemos that commercial web redistribution of Output is allowed.
routes.web_fit: High-poly output; heavy decimation and atlas re-bake needed (as R3).
routes.risks:
- Ambiguous ownership.
- Fused foliage.
- Download-based credit costs.
- Terms are undated.

routes.name: R6. CSM Cube and Luma Genie (not viable today)
routes.what: Two earlier image- or text-to-3D services.
routes.realism: Unknown; a reviewer says CSM output is a 'chaotic web of polygons' with poor thin geometry (https://www.3daistudio.com/blog/top-csm-ai-alternatives-for-3d-model-generation).
routes.licence:
Not obtainable.
- CSM: Google's acquisition closed 24 Jan 2026 (https://aihola.com/article/google-acquires-common-sense-machines), and csm.ai failed DNS on 2026-10-17.
- Luma: https://lumalabs.ai/genie no longer describes 3D generation.
routes.cost: Last known CSM prices: Maker US$20/mo for 100 credits; Creative Pro US$60/mo for 400 credits. Luma: unknown.
routes.risks: Service availability; no legible current terms.

routes.name: R7. TRELLIS and TRELLIS.2 (Microsoft, open weights)
routes.what: Open-weight image-to-3D, run on a rented Linux GPU or the public Hugging Face Space (huggingface.co/spaces/microsoft/TRELLIS.2). TRELLIS.2 is a 4B-parameter model using an 'O-Voxel' representation, with GLB output carrying base colour, roughness, metallic and opacity.
routes.species_coverage: The best AI chance for broad-leaf clumps: hosta, maybe daylily, hydrangea heads, plus the clipped-evergreen shells. Still no realistic path for needles (pines, spruce, yew), grasses, ferns or fine-textured shrubs.
routes.realism:
The TRELLIS.2 README claims open surfaces such as leaves and clothing, and non-manifold geometry, are handled 'without lossy conversion' (https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2). No foliage benchmark exists.
The GLB is exported OPAQUE by default, with alpha kept in the texture but inactive, so leaf cutouts need manual material work.
Textures are 4096 px, generated from a single image.
routes.licence:
- Model and code: MIT (https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2). The README notes that nvdiffrast and nvdiffrec are governed by their own licences.
- nvdiffrast: NVIDIA Source Code License (1-Way Commercial). §3.3 limits use to non-commercial research or evaluation (https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/blob/main/LICENSE.txt).
- TRELLIS v1: most code and models MIT. Its diffoctreerast derives from Inria's diff-gaussian-rasterization; the Inria licence is non-commercial, research and evaluation only (https://github.com/graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting/blob/main/LICENSE.md).
- The MIT licence puts no limit on outputs. Running the NC-dependent pipeline for a business is the problem unless those parts are replaced.
- The Hugging Face Space's terms were not checked.
routes.cost:
- Software: free.
- Hardware: TRELLIS.2 needs an NVIDIA GPU with 24 GB+ (verified on A100/H100, Linux only); TRELLIS needs 16 GB+. The owner's RTX 5070 has 12 GB, which is not enough.
- RunPod: A100 80GB about US$1.19–1.89/hr; RTX 4090 about US$0.34–0.74/hr; L40S about US$0.79–0.99/hr (https://www.runpod.io/gpu-cloud/pricing).
- Speed: about 60 s per asset at 1536³ on an H100.
- A 26-species test is roughly 2–4 GPU-hours plus setup.
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve metered GPU rental.
- Approve weight and tool downloads (several GB).
- Or approve uploading images to the public Hugging Face Space.
- Accept or resolve the nvdiffrast NC issue.
- Note: the owner keeps ComfyUI paused on purpose, so any local run is a separate decision.
routes.web_fit:
- High-poly GLB with 4K textures.
- Decimate and re-bake into atlases, as R3.
- Opacity must be rewired by hand for leaf alpha.
routes.risks:
- Licence (NC dependencies).
- Linux/CUDA setup effort.
- Foliage quality unproven.
- Metered spend.

routes.name: R8. Hunyuan3D 2.1 (local, open weights) and Hunyuan 3.x (API)
routes.what:
Tencent's image-to-3D model.
- Version 2.1 can run locally: shape-only generation fits 12 GB.
- Versions 3.0/3.1 Pro appear to be API-only via third-party hosts.
routes.species_coverage: Same as R3: shells for clipped evergreens and flower heads only.
routes.realism: No foliage tests were found. Per a search excerpt of SAM3D-Part (arXiv 2609.15639), structures thinner than a voxel are lost or merged in the Hunyuan3D ShapeVAE.
routes.licence:
Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.1 Community License, released 13 Jun 2025 (https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1/blob/main/LICENSE), paraphrased:
- §1(l) Territory: worldwide except the EU, UK and South Korea. Canada is included.
- §6(d): Tencent claims no rights in Outputs.
- §5(b): Outputs must not be used to improve other AI models.
- §4: a separate licence is needed above 1M monthly active users.
- Exhibit A item 12: machine-generated content placed in public must be expressly and conspicuously identified as machine-generated. This directly conflicts with an unlabelled photoreal public site.
routes.cost:
- Local 2.1: free. VRAM is about 10 GB for shape (fits the RTX 5070), about 21 GB for texture (does not fit), about 29 GB for both. Texturing would need a rented GPU (see R7 prices).
- 3.x API: about US$0.015 per model on fal, or Layer's '21 per generation' (both third-party, unverified).
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve weight download and install.
- Decide on ComfyUI.
- Accept the licence.
- Decide on conspicuous 'AI-generated' labelling of any plant made this way.
routes.web_fit: Same as R3. Locally the output is untextured, so photo textures would need projecting by hand.
routes.risks:
- Labelling obligation.
- Territory clause if the site serves EU or UK users (it is accessible there).
- §5(b) against GitHub's AI-training grant on public repos (minor).
- Fused foliage.

routes.name: R9. Stable Fast 3D and SPAR3D (Stability AI, open weights)
routes.what: Fast single-image (512×512) to low-poly, UV-unwrapped, de-lit mesh with per-object roughness and metallic values.
routes.species_coverage: None usable beyond far, opaque hulls.
routes.realism: The lowest detail of all the AI options. The model card notes a relatively low polygon count; foliage comes out as lumps (https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-fast-3d).
routes.licence:
Stability AI Community License, updated 5 Jul 2024 (https://stability.ai/community-license-agreement), paraphrased:
- Free commercial use while annual revenue is at or below US$1M; above that an Enterprise licence is required.
- §IV(c)(iii): you own the outputs.
- Outputs may not be used to create or improve foundational generative AI models.
- The Hugging Face download is gated behind sharing contact details.
routes.cost: Free if Golden Maple's annual revenue is US$1M or less (the owner must confirm). Runs locally on 12 GB (estimated).
routes.owner_actions:
- Confirm the revenue threshold.
- Approve the gated download and local install.
routes.web_fit: Already low-poly. Textures need re-baking into atlases.
routes.risks:
- Revenue threshold.
- Very low fidelity.
- No real value over the procedural hulls.

routes.name: R10. Owner photo capture programme (RECOMMENDED primary source)
routes.what:
The owner photographs the exact cultivars he sells at nursery yards, his own installs and client gardens (with permission):
(a) Specimens of leaves, sprays, flower heads and plumes on a white or black card or a light box, in overcast light or with cross-polarised light, with a colour chart in frame.
(b) Eye-level whole-plant reference shots with a scale stick.
(c) Bark close-ups.
(d) Optionally, turntable sets of potted plants for R13 and R15.
The photos feed the procedural plan's atlases in place of SVG masks, CC0 tiles or AI images.
routes.species_coverage:
All 26 at species and cultivar level: Smaragd, Annabelle, Karl Foerster, and whichever panicle hydrangea, spirea, ninebark, daylily, catmint, salvia, switchgrass and little bluestem cultivars he installs.
Season, from mid-October 2026:
- Shootable now: Colorado blue spruce, white pine, Smaragd, boxwood, yew, all bark, and the three grasses in their autumn state.
- Hydrangea heads are dried now. Deciduous leaves and perennial flowers need about mid-May to September 2027, unless he has archived summer close-ups.
routes.realism:
The highest ceiling: real texture grain, true cultivar colour and real venation, which is what removes the CG or AI look.
- Game-art practice: shoot in a light box with cross-polarised light for albedo (https://polycount.com/discussion/comment/2686865; Epic's guide at https://udn.epicgames.com/Three/TakingBetterPhotosForTextures.html).
- One ArtStation project scanned ivy leaves under multi-angle light to derive normals and roughness (https://pangea.artstation.com/projects/58dPBz).
- Landscaping photo-imaging software itself relies on real plant photos (PRO Landscape, about 18,000 items).
routes.licence:
The owner's own copyright; no third-party terms apply.
- This checkout has no LICENSE file, so committed images default to all rights reserved.
- GitHub's terms: making a repo public allows others to view and fork it, and §D.4 lets GitHub use content to train its AI features (https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service).
- Photos taken on nursery or client property need permission. Keep people, house numbers and plates out of frame.
routes.cost:
- US$0 with his phone.
- Optional Calibrite ColorChecker Classic Mini, about US$74 list, or Passport Photo 2, about US$119 list (Glazer's, https://www.glazerscamera.com/products/colorchecker-passport-photo-2).
- Polarising film or filter: about US$20–60 (estimate, not researched).
- Time: about 1–2 hours per species including travel.
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve the shot list.
- Arrange nursery and client permissions.
- Shoot, or delegate to crew.
- Deliver original-resolution files.
- Give botanical sign-off.
- Optionally approve the ColorChecker purchase.
routes.web_fit: Same atlases and budgets as PLAN.md: 1024²–2048² shared atlases, about 10–11 MiB GPU as RGBA8 or about 2.7 MiB with KTX2. Phone photos at 12–48 MP give native resolution, so no upscaling is needed. No runtime change; works at every LOD and in showcase LOD0 and Photo mode.
routes.risks:
- The summer-state gap until May 2027.
- Weather and white balance.
- Owner time.
- Nursery stock differs from mature installed plants (use install photos for whole-plant reference).
- Inconsistent capture unless a simple rig and chart are used.

routes.name: R11. Free and open AI processing toolchain for photos (matting, de-lighting, normals, depth, upscaling)
routes.what:
Build-time tools that turn R10 photos, or approved R1 images, into clean PBR atlas cells:
- Matting: BiRefNet / BiRefNet_HR-matting.
- Albedo, roughness and metallic: Marigold IID-appearance.
- Depth for impostor parallax or shadow proxies: Depth Anything V2 Small.
- Height, normal, AO and seamless tiling: Materialize (Windows) or DeepBump (Blender add-on or CLI).
- Bark and mulch upscaling: Real-ESRGAN ncnn-vulkan portable.
routes.species_coverage: A tool, not a source: applies to all 26.
routes.realism:
Improves realism by removing baked light, specular highlights and alpha fringes; it adds no botanical fidelity.
- Upscalers invent detail, so never use them on leaves where venation matters.
- Treat Marigold IID splits of leaf translucency as unverified and check them visually.
routes.licence:
- BiRefNet: code MIT (https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet); BiRefNet_HR-matting weights MIT per the model-card metadata, trained at 2048² (https://huggingface.co/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet_HR-matting).
- Marigold: code Apache-2.0, models RAIL++-M, an open licence with use restrictions (https://github.com/prs-eth/Marigold).
- Depth Anything V2: Small is Apache-2.0; Base, Large and Giant are CC-BY-NC-4.0, so use Small only (https://github.com/DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2).
- Materialize: GPL-3 (http://boundingboxsoftware.com/materialize/).
- DeepBump: GPL-3 (https://github.com/HugoTini/DeepBump). The GPL covers the tools, not the images they produce.
- Real-ESRGAN: code BSD-3; the README does not state the model-weight licence (https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN).
- EXCLUDED: BRIA RMBG-2.0, CC BY-NC 4.0, commercial use needs an agreement (https://huggingface.co/briaai/RMBG-2.0).
- EXCLUDED: Ubisoft CHORD, research-only licence (https://blog.comfy.org/p/ubisoft-open-sources-the-chord-model).
routes.cost: US$0. All should run on the owner's RTX 5070 12 GB (estimated) or CPU.
routes.owner_actions:
- Approve each download: tool binaries and weights, with source and size listed first.
- Approve a local Python environment. ComfyUI stays paused; run standalone.
routes.web_fit: Build-time only, adding zero runtime bytes. Slots into the planned cutout, dilation and calibration step.
routes.risks:
- RAIL++-M use restrictions must be carried.
- Model artefacts in albedo or normals.
- Real-ESRGAN weight licence not stated on the README; check the model card before use.
- Python dependency upkeep.

routes.name: R12. Adobe Substance 3D Sampler (paid AI image-to-material)
routes.what: Sampler's Image to Material AI, available since 4.2, produces base colour, roughness and normal maps from one photo, and includes tiling and de-light tools. A polished, one-stop alternative to R11 for bark, mulch, soil and leaf-material calibration.
routes.species_coverage: A tool for all 26. Strongest for bark and ground tiles, weaker for alpha leaf clusters.
routes.realism: Industry-standard results on surface materials. It adds no botanical fidelity.
routes.licence:
The Adobe General Terms were not fetched this session. Adobe's usual position is that it claims no ownership of user content; verify before purchase.
Plan details: https://blog.adobe.com/en/publish/2025/02/20/substance-3d-innovations-pricing-updates.
routes.cost:
- Substance 3D Texturing plan (Designer, Painter, Sampler; 25 generative credits/mo): US$24.99/mo, or US$17.49/mo on an annual plan billed monthly.
- Collection: US$59.99/mo.
routes.web_fit: Build-time only; exports standard PNG/EXR maps into the atlases.
routes.risks:
- Subscription lock-in.
- Generative-credit limits.
- R11 covers most needs for free.

routes.name: R13. Photo view-set impostors (RPC-style) from owner turntable photos
routes.species_coverage: Containerised or B&B stock: boxwood, yew, Smaragd (small sizes), both hydrangeas, spirea, ninebark, dogwood, lilac (small), all perennials, the three grasses, ostrich fern and hosta. Not the trees: a 15 ft specimen cannot be put on a turntable.
routes.licence: Owner-owned photos; processing tools as R11. No third-party terms.
routes.cost:
- Turntable and backdrop: about US$0–100 (estimate, not researched).
- About 30 minutes per species at a nursery.
routes.owner_actions:
- Nursery permission.
- Capture sessions.
- Approve a new runtime shader in the lazy Landscape3D chunk.
routes.web_fit:
- About 5.6 MiB per species for 8 views at 256×512 RGBA8 with mips; roughly a quarter to an eighth of that with KTX2.
- A new 2–4 KB shader.
- Alpha-tested overdraw on phones.
- Not LOD0, so absent from showcase stills, which force LOD0. Not usable in three-gpu-pathtracer Photo mode except as flat cards.
routes.risks:
- Lighting and scale mismatch.
- View popping.
- Capture effort.
- PLAN.md currently excludes impostors.

routes.name: R14. Octahedral impostors baked from our own 3D species models (phone LOD2)
routes.what:
At build time, bake a hemi-octahedral atlas of albedo, normal and depth from each species' LOD0 model, then render it as a 2-triangle impostor. Tools:
- agargaro/octahedral-impostor (three.js, MIT, marked WIP: https://github.com/agargaro/octahedral-impostor).
- Blender add-on Imposter Cards (https://superhivemarket.com/products/imposter-cards-nacho-time/docs).
- Houdini Labs Impostor Texture.
- The Godot Octahedral Impostor add-on is a technique reference: 144 views with depth and normals.
routes.species_coverage: All 26: any species that has a LOD0 model.
routes.realism: As real as the source model at distance. Baked normals let DeckCraft's sun relight it, which photo impostors cannot do. It adds no realism by itself.
routes.licence: Own output. agargaro is MIT. Imposter Cards is a paid royalty-free tool, and its output is ours (its terms were not fetched).
routes.cost: US$0 with agargaro (MIT), or US$25 (standard) / US$50 (Advanced) for Imposter Cards.
routes.owner_actions: Approve the dependency or add-on purchase, and the deviation from PLAN.md, which uses a billboard-cloud LOD2 and excludes impostors.
routes.web_fit:
- 1024² with 8×8 frames (128 px): about 5.3 MiB albedo plus about 5.3 MiB normal and depth per species as RGBA8 with mips; about 1.4 MiB each with KTX2.
- 2 triangles per plant; ideal for the constrained tier and the 273-plant estate background.
- A runtime shader of a few KB in the lazy chunk.
routes.risks:
- The library is WIP.
- Texture memory if many species share a scene.
- Parallax artefacts up close.
- Only worth doing if the billboard cloud looks flat.

routes.name: R15. Gaussian-splat captures of real specimens (hero or showcase only)
routes.what:
1. Phone video or photos walking around a real specimen.
2. Train a splat locally with Brush (Apache-2.0, Windows, WebGPU).
3. Crop, clean and compress to SPZ or SOG.
4. Render with three.js r186's native GaussianSplat (three 0.186.0, 8 Sep 2026; the repo is on 0.185) or Spark 2.x (MIT, World Labs).
Optional splat-to-mesh conversion via LeafFit, Eurographics 2026: about 1.13 MB mesh against 38–47 MB alternatives (https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2602.11577). LeafFit is a prototype with no LICENSE file, built on Inria's non-commercial rasterizer, so it is not usable commercially as-is (https://github.com/netbeifeng/leaf_fit).
routes.species_coverage: Any specimen he can walk around: best for shrubs, perennials, grasses and small evergreens; trees only in open sites. Shows that exact plant, at its actual size and cultivar.
routes.realism:
The most photographic of all routes for thin foliage.
- The LeafFit authors say 3DGS is particularly effective for vegetation with thin leaves and intricate silhouettes.
- ArcGIS docs cite individual leaves and dense vegetation as a strength.
But:
- Lighting is baked from the capture day.
- Splats do not cast or receive DeckCraft sun shadows.
- They cannot be relit to the HDRI; relighting research still struggles with shadows (PRTGS, arXiv 2408.03538).
- three-gpu-pathtracer Photo mode does not render them.
- Wind blurs leaves during capture.
routes.licence:
Owner-owned captures. Brush Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/ArthurBrussee/brush). Spark MIT (https://github.com/sparkjsdev/spark). three.js MIT.
Avoid:
- Inria-based trainers (non-commercial licence).
- Postshot Free, which is non-commercial. Postshot Indie allows commercial use, but its price was not captured (https://activation.jawset.com/shop/pricing).
routes.cost:
- US$0 with a phone and Brush, plus capture time.
- Postshot Indie: price unknown.
- Upgrading three to r186, or adding Spark to the lazy chunk, is engineering effort.
routes.owner_actions:
- Capture sessions with permission.
- Approve the Brush download.
- Decide whether a hero-splat mode is wanted, since it cannot appear in path-traced stills.
routes.web_fit:
- 100k–500k splats per plant. Raw size is about 236 B per splat with spherical harmonics (Vulkan sample docs), so 24–118 MB per plant.
- SPZ or SOG compression brings that to roughly 3–20 MB (estimated).
- Depth sorting on each camera move costs time on phones.
- r186 core has no LOD or streaming yet (https://radiancefields.com/platforms/three-js).
- Impossible for the 273-plant showcase, so high tier, 1–3 hero plants at most.
routes.risks:
- Lighting and shadow mismatch beside mesh plants.
- Missing from Photo mode.
- File size.
- Phone performance.
- Style clash with neighbouring mesh plants.

routes.name: R16. AI-generated orbit video (Veo in Gemini, Sora or ChatGPT video) reconstructed into a splat or mesh
routes.what: Generate a turntable video of each species in the browser, then reconstruct it with Brush or photogrammetry.
routes.species_coverage: All 26 in theory; the forms the model invents become the asset.
routes.realism: Poor. 2026 research (OrbitForge, VidSplat) reports that generated videos are not 3D-consistent: camera motion is hard to control, coverage is partial, and frames are inconsistent over time (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.11424; https://papers.cool/arxiv/2606.24799). Foliage flicker makes noisy splats, and on top of that come the botanical-fidelity problems of R1.
routes.licence: As R1. The vendor terms give the user ownership of outputs (Google: https://policies.google.com/terms; OpenAI: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use). Veo output carries SynthID.
routes.cost: Video quotas on Google AI Pro or Ultra and ChatGPT Plus or Pro (see R1 prices). Daily video limits are low.
routes.owner_actions: Approve each video generation. Not recommended.
routes.web_fit: Inherits R15's splat limits, or R3's mesh clean-up.
routes.risks:
- Invented botany.
- 3D artefacts.
- High effort for a low-quality result.
- All of R15's runtime issues.
